description:
FILED s470bi (Opus, 2026-09-05) after losing two gate runs to it.  An
INFRASTRUCTURE bug, not a compiler one, and it costs a whole gate each time.

`p-load-module-cached` keys a cached module transpile under
`~/.pcl-cache/<hash>.lisp`, and the hash is mixed with
`*pcl-cache-generation*` -- a HAND-MAINTAINED STRING in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp.
That string says what a session INTENDED; it does not identify the compiler
that wrote the file.  Two consequences, both measured in one session:

  (1) A SIBLING WORKTREE WITH THE SAME STRING SHARES THE CACHE.  s470bi and
      another agent's worktree both carried "v2-700".  A gate row died with

          The function |File::Path|::%p-sort-classic is undefined
            ... in "/home/bernt/.pcl-cache/0A1C6FD58D93AF7F.lisp"

      and `%p-sort-classic` does not exist anywhere in s470bi's tree -- the
      entry was written by the sibling's compiler and loaded by this runtime.
      The row passes standalone.  Parallel Opus agents are the normal working
      mode now (rounds 21-24), so this is not a corner.

  (2) A STOPPED SESSION'S ENTRIES OUTLIVE ITS COMPILER.  s469bi ran at v2-690
      on a base that predates #1035's p-sub facts plist; s470bi resumed the
      same worktree at the same string with #1035 merged, and every gate file
      that loads a module died at

          p-sub: unknown fact key p-args-body ... the set is closed: (...)

      The only cure was `rm -f ~/.pcl-cache/*.lisp` plus a new string -- and
      choosing the next round number is what walked into (1).

THE SAVED-CORE CACHE DOES NOT HAVE THIS PROBLEM.  Since s439 it is named by a
HASH of the runtime source + `sbcl --version` + ~/.sbclrc + the runtime's
ABSOLUTE PATH (so a worktree gets its own), and CLAUDE.md can therefore say
"it cannot be stale: an edit makes a new core and prunes the old".  The module
cache should be keyed the same way.

FIX SHAPE (untried): mix the same content hash the core cache uses into the
module-cache key -- the runtime source's digest plus the compiler's
(`Pl/**`), or at minimum the runtime path, so two trees cannot collide.  The
generation string can then stay as the human-readable stamp it is (line 1 of
each artifact, `Pl/t/artifact-staleness-01.t`) without being load-bearing for
correctness.  Cost: hashing `Pl/**` once per process; the core cache already
pays the equivalent.

INTERIM RULE for a launcher (s425's, restated with its reason): give each
agent a generation string with a GAP above main AND above every sibling in
flight, and tell a RESUMED agent that its predecessor's string is poisoned.

=== DONE (s473i) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-08.

The key is now sxhash(<module path> | *pcl-cache-generation* | "v2" |
p-compiler-stamp).  THE RULE IS THE ONE THE TREE ALREADY HAD â grep before
designing: Pl::ProtoCache::_compiler_stamp (#560) keys its prototype memo on
the Pl/ directory's ABSOLUTE PATH plus every Pl/**.pm's mtime+size, and its
POD already says "this is also what keeps two worktrees that happen to share a
generation string from reading each other's entries".  The runtime mirrors
that rule and adds pl2cl itself (the file this side SPAWNS, which ProtoCache
running inside it cannot see).

STAT AND NOT CONTENT, measured rather than assumed â the task's own fix shape
and the brief both guessed content at ~5 ms:
    MD5 over the 2.24 MB of Pl/**.pm + pl2cl    14.7 ms
    the stat stamp (41 paths)                    1.5 ms
paid once per process, and only by a process that loads a module
(p-compute-cache-path is its only caller).  What content would catch and this
does not: a compiler file whose SIZE and MTIME are both unchanged while its
bytes differ.  `git checkout` does not produce that (it stamps every file it
writes with the current time), and #1261's argument against mtimes is about a
DEPENDENCY â a file the user edits and git restores â not about the PCL tree.

Computed at FIRST USE and memoised for the process, never while the runtime
loads (on the normal path that is when a saved CORE is built, and Pl/ can be
edited afterwards); an sb-ext:*init-hooks* entry clears the memo at image
start, the #1303 shape.  When no compiler root can be derived the answer is
the literal "no-compiler-root" = exactly the pre-#1119 behaviour, never
weaker.

`pcl --cache-info` now prints compiler root, compiler stamp and runtime
identity.

Guards: Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t 55 -> 59 rows â two fake compiler trees
asked of the runtime itself, ONE FRESH PROCESS PER ANSWER so the rows do not
depend on the memo variable existing (a guard must DISAGREE on the base, not
error there).  On the a9f2a264 extraction the two claims fail (different trees
get the same key; touching a Pl/*.pm does not change it) while "the same tree
keeps its key" passes there as it must.

CONSEQUENCE to expect, and it is the point: editing anything under Pl/ now
invalidates the module cache, as a generation bump always did.  The gate and
the sweep were both run on a cold module cache after the change (gate 96 s
wall, sweep 2m35) and neither moved.
subject: The module cache is keyed by the HAND-MAINTAINED *pcl-cache-generation* string, so two worktrees with the same string silently share (and corrupt) each other's cached module transpiles -- two gate runs lost in s470bi.  The saved-CORE cache is content-keyed and immune; key the module cache the same way
